stem: What is the average N–O bond order in the resonance hybrid of the nitrate ion, $\text{NO}_3^-$?

verdicts.working: Each resonance structure has one N=O bond and two N–O bonds, so the average is (2+1+1)/3 = 4/3.

working:
Each canonical form has one N=O bond and two N–O bonds.
Average bond order $=\dfrac{2+1+1}{3}=\dfrac{4}{3}$.

Independent check: Each resonance structure has one N=O bond and two N–O bonds, so the average is (2+1+1)/3 = 4/3.
solution: Each resonance structure has one N=O double bond and two N–O single bonds. Thus, the average N–O bond order is $$\frac{2+1+1}{3}=\frac{4}{3}.$$
